limitations: AI-generated static source analysis. Confirm the affected version, platform, update channel, and cited control flow before relying on this classification.

later_review_audit.description: Buttercup's desktop updater checks the buttercup-desktop GitHub feed about every 30 minutes, leaves electron-updater auto-retrieval disabled until the user starts a retrieval, and installs a retrieved update through the install action. Release scripts publish SHA-512 metadata and invoke a Windows signing hook; this review does not establish application-pinned runtime verification.

fields.label: auto
fields.value: auto chk (every 30 min via `setDelayedInterval`) + notify; `autoUpdater.autoDownload = false` so download/install require explicit user action (`startUpdate()` / `installUpdate()` → `quitAndInstall()`)

fields.label: transport
fields.value: HTTPS via GitHub Releases feed (`electron-updater`'s `github` provider, owner `buttercup`, repo `buttercup-desktop`); TLS validation ENFORCED (no `rejectUnauthorized`/TLS-bypass code found in source/)

fields.label: manifest_signed
fields.value: N (electron-updater's `latest.yml`/`latest-mac.yml` manifest is plain YAML with a SHA-512 field, not separately signed)

fields.label: payload_verification
fields.value: hash-from-manifest (SHA-512 of the downloaded installer checked against the value in `latest*.yml`) + OS-code-signing (electron-updater's default `verifyUpdateCodeSignature`/Squirrel.Mac behavior requires the downloaded installer's Authenticode/code-signing identity to match the running app on Windows/macOS)

fields.label: verifying_key_source
fields.value: n/a for the manifest hash (unsigned, trust = GitHub HTTPS); code-signing identity check relies on the OS certificate store / running app's own signing cert, not an app-embedded key
